prs.title: fix(bindings): bind one BLE service instance per link on a phone running several SDK apps
prs.body:
## Summary

Two copies of one app could stop finding each other over Bluetooth as soon as a second app built on this SDK was installed on either phone. Uninstalling the other app and toggling Bluetooth on both phones was the only recovery.

**Why.** Every SDK app registers the same GATT service, and iOS and Android merge every app's service into one device-wide GATT database. A phone running a chat app and a game therefore presents **two instances of the service behind one BLE connection**, each serving a different identity. Both bridges assumed one:

- **iOS** discovered characteristics on every instance and read DEVICE_ID and IDENTITY from each into the same per-peripheral slot, then cross-checked whichever pair landed. The peer was refused as a mismatch, or announced under the other app's identity, at random.
- **Android** used `gatt.getService(serviceUuid)` at every step, which returns the first instance: always the app that registered first.

**The fix.** Each app now serves an 8-byte tag in a new, optional characteristic `6E400005-B5A3-F393-E0A9-E50E24DCCA9E`: the first eight bytes of `SHA-256("offline-protocol-ble-app-tag-v1" || 0x00 || appId)`. A central that finds several instances reads their tags and picks one with `BleServiceInstanceSelection`:

1. the first instance serving its own tag;
2. else, if exactly one serves no tag, that one (a build that predates the tag);
3. else the first instance, which is what it did before.

The unchanged handshake, subscription and writes then run on that instance only. The choice never refuses a link: relay forwarding is keyed on the recipient, never the app, so a phone running only other SDK apps still carries our traffic and stays a neighbour.

**One link, one peer, deliberately.** Announcing every instance as its own peer was considered and rejected for this PR. The peripheral role attributes an inbound write to a sender by the link it arrived on, so a second identity on one link would have its hop-0 control frames refused by `validate_transport_sender`. Doing that properly needs a core change to accept a set of verified senders per link. A per-app service UUID was also rejected: it is a wire break, and it would stop cross-app relaying outright.

## What does not change

**A peer running one SDK app takes exactly the path it took before.** There is no probe, no binding and no tag read, and every service lookup falls back to `services.first` / `gatt.getService` as it always did. That is every deployment that works today.

- The new characteristic is appended **after** the existing three, so their attribute handles do not move for a central holding a cached GATT table.
- No UDL change, no engine change, no event change, no config change. The tag comes from the `appId` each app already passes.
- An older SDK build serves no tag and ignores the new characteristic. It keeps its old behaviour, and until it upgrades it cannot pick its own counterpart on a multi-app phone.

## Related issues

None filed. Found while debugging a game built on the SDK that stopped pairing once a second SDK app was installed on the test phones.

## Type of change

- [x] `fix` — bug fix
- [x] `docs` — documentation only

## Checklist

- [x] `cargo fmt --all -- --check` passes
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` passes
- [x] `cargo test` passes for the two crates touched (`offline-protocol-uniffi`: 136, `offline-protocol-transport`: 295 + 5). No other crate is changed; the full workspace run is left to CI.
- [x] `cargo-deny` is satisfied (no dependency changes)
- [x] Commits follow Conventional Commits
- [x] Docs / `CHANGELOG.md` updated
- [x] No new `unsafe`
- [x] UDL unchanged, so no binding regeneration

Bridge checks, since `cargo test` proves nothing about the bridges (C9):

- [x] `swift test --package-path bindings/react-native/ios`: 360/360 (13 new)
- [x] Android `:offlineprotocol:testDebugUnitTest` in a clean copy of the CI harness: 495/495 (14 new). Kotlin warning count unchanged versus `main`.
- [x] iOS typecheck with CI's file list, and of all 40 hand-written sources including `OfflineProtocolModule.swift` (via the `BRIDGE_MAINTENANCE.md` recipe, with a negative control that calls the old two-argument `BleManager` init and fails).
- [ ] **Two-phone matrix on real hardware** (CI runs neither bridge's GATT code). See "Notes for reviewers".

## Breaking changes

None. The GATT change is additive: an optional characteristic that old centrals never request.

## Notes for reviewers

**Where to look.**

- `ios/BleManager.swift`:
  - The gate is one line at the top of `didDiscoverCharacteristicsFor`, **above** the subscribe, so an unchosen instance is neither subscribed to nor read.
  - The probe/selection helpers sit together under `// MARK: Service instance selection`.
  - Every service lookup goes through `handshakeService(on:)`.
- `android/.../ble/CentralGattClient.kt`: the tag phase slots into the existing one-GATT-op-per-callback chain. It sits between the MTU exchange and the device-id read, at all three MTU exits (`onMtuChanged`, its watchdog, and a refused `requestMtu`), via `readServiceInstanceTagsIfChoosing`. Every later lookup goes through `handshakeService(gatt)`, including the facade's write path.

**Threading (iOS).** CoreBluetooth delegates run on main (`queue: nil`), but the send path runs on `fragmentQueue`. The per-link binding (`.choosing` / `.bound(CBService)` / `.dropping`) is therefore behind its own `NSLock`. While a link is choosing, the send path writes nothing. Without that, a transient reconnect keeps the old peer-id mapping and would write to `services.first` before the re-handshake.

**A choice lasts one connection.** Selection state is cleared on connect, on adopting an already-connected peripheral, on disconnect and on stop. If the bound instance disappears mid-link (its app quit), iOS drops the link and re-handshakes rather than rebinding. That way the identity a link was announced under and the instance its frames go to can never be two different apps. `didModifyServices` is newly implemented for this, and it returns immediately for a single-instance link. Android needs no equivalent for sends: its write path already waits for the CCCD ack on the chosen instance.

**Pinned from Rust.** `react_native_ble_binds_one_service_instance_per_link` pins:

- the UUID literal in both bridges to the new `BLE_APP_TAG_CHAR_UUID` constant;
- the tag domain and the shared test vectors across both platforms;
- the iOS gate above the subscribe;
- exactly one first-instance lookup per bridge;
- all three Android MTU exits.

It was mutation-tested: removing the iOS gate, removing one Android MTU exit, or reverting the facade to `gatt.getService(SERVICE_UUID)` each fails it. The existing identity-binding and idempotent-discovery guards pass unchanged.

**Security.** The tag is unsigned. Any key can sign any tag, so a signature would add nothing the Identity characteristic does not already prove. A co-installed app can serve another app's tag and be chosen in its place, but it is still bound under its **own** proved address. The tag is also readable in range, as a digest of the app id. Both are written up as residual risk R15 in the threat model.

**Two-phone matrix to run before merge**, using diagnostics that log `BLE service instance chosen` with the reason:

- [ ] A: game only; B: game + another SDK app, both on this branch → pair on the first attempt, twice, and again after a Bluetooth toggle (`reason: same_app`)
- [ ] B: game on this branch + another SDK app on an older SDK → game still pairs (`same_app`, or `sole_untagged` from the older app's side)
- [ ] B: only another SDK app → game still lists it as a neighbour, as before (`first_instance`)
- [ ] A and B: game only → unchanged; no `BLE service instance chosen` line and no tag read
- [ ] Uninstall the other app on B mid-session, without toggling Bluetooth → game keeps or regains the link

**Docs.**

- `docs/spec/ble-framing.md` now specifies App tag and the selection rule. It also fixes the stale "three characteristics" line that sat above a four-row table.
- The threat model gains R15.
- Bridge rule C5 lists the tag as the tenth hand-mirrored set.
- The React Native README gains a troubleshooting entry.

**Out of scope, noted.** `docs/mesh.md` and the React Native README still say mesh metadata rides in advertisement service data, which neither platform does. The engine delivers frames whose `app_id` differs from its own, and `neighbor_discovered` cannot say which app a peer runs. Each would be its own change.
